pr_title: [ActiveAESink] Improves sinks enumeration names and fallback logic when exact sink name not exists
pr_body:
## Description
- Improves `CAESinkFactory::ParseDevice` returning values in a struct instead parameters by reference. Also avoids use same "device" parameter as input/output which is confusing and requires make a copy to avoids get overwrited in some places.
- Appends sink friendly name to sink string when is different from sink name. e.g:

  Before
  `WASAPI:{B12C1A75-F8A8-4071-8CFB-A285C619CCB8}`
    
  After
  `WASAPI:{B12C1A75-F8A8-4071-8CFB-A285C619CCB8}:HDMI - DENON-AVR (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)`

- When open sink by name (GUID in Windows) and exact match not found, fallback using friendly name.
- Saved settings are not modified unless user opens audio settings.
- When user opens audio settings current device name is "upgraded" and saved in settings, adding friendly name if available.
- Even if current device GUID not exist in system anymore, current setting is not lost because fallback to a device with same friendly name and saved as current "new" device.
- Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21852


## Motivation and context
On Windows sink names are GUIDs and these may change sporadically with Windows Updates or audio drivers updates. When this happens, current logic is fallback to first audio device in list and this breaks passthrough probably because changes from `WASAPI:x` to `DIRECTSOUND:y`

For some users this is just a Kodi bug "Kodi changes sporadically to DIRECTSOUND and breaks passthrough". See https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21852 and https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/22021

Or in forum: https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=373640 or https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=372205

This PR appends friendly device name to setting and, in this way, if GUID changes, same device can be still referenced by friendly name e.g.:

Device saved in settings is:
 `WASAPI:{B12C1A75-F8A8-4071-8CFB-A285C619CCB8}:HDMI - DENON-AVR (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)`

But current system device is:
`WASAPI:{555C1A75-F8A8-4071-8CFB-A285C619CCB8}:HDMI - DENON-AVR (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)`

Kodi can continue operate in this way and saved setting is not altered but a WARNING log message warns of this situation.
When the user realizes (if it happens) he can fix it in settings and if not, nothing happens... the next time the user enters in settings it will fix itself for the simple fact that the current setting has changed and the settings are saved when changes.

Since the current setting can only be one of the list and in the list there are only the devices that currently exist in the system.

After this, "new" saved setting is:
`WASAPI:{555C1A75-F8A8-4071-8CFB-A285C619CCB8}:HDMI - DENON-AVR (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)`

And the warning message in the logs disappears.

All this is designed for backward compatibility, that is, it is not mandatory that the settings have the friendly name. And it is also not expected that the audio device will change by the fact of starting to use Kodi with these changes nor is it expected any significant change in the operation except the improvement when the same exact device does not exist.

Even in the case that the setting does not (yet) have the friendly name there are some improvements in the logic: it will always be preferred to change to a device of the same driver first e.g. from `WASAPI:x` to `WASAPI:default` instead of switching to the first random device (DIRECTSOUND).

Please review commits separately as has useful descriptions.


## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested Windows x64 also in Shield (to look for side effects)

## What is the effect on users?
Avoids in some systems sporadically audio device settings are lost because Windows Updates or audio drivers updates.
In general it improves (much) the fallback logic when the current audio device is not available.

I don't really have time to review but I did something similar earlier this year. Maybe there is some similarities -> https://github.com/lrusak/xbmc/commit/ab50136ff883cefe02034a15d33c9acbb8d61fe5

I also had some other AE stuff here if you are interested -> https://github.com/lrusak/xbmc/commits/ae-device-selection

Very good improvement for Windows, much better than having the sound device suddenly defaulting to first directsound output after a driver upgrade.

At a high level, looks fine by itself to me but I don't know how well it fits with AE's design.
The logic to find a sink with same friendly name or first/default sink of same driver is duplicated in the sink opening and the audio setting filler. Maybe could be solved by generalizing the arguments and extracting to shared functions.

At a low level, a few style improvements if you have the time:
- A new function like `std::vector<AE::AESinkInfo> CActiveAESink::GetDriverSinks(std::string_view driver) would help remove many copies (new and existing) of code similar to
```
for (auto itt = m_sinkInfoList.begin(); itt != m_sinkInfoList.end(); ++itt)
  {
    if (dev.driver == itt->m_sinkName)
```
- A proper split function in `CAESinkFactory::ParseDevice()`, like in commit https://github.com/lrusak/xbmc/commit/040262f0367127a6634b0ab821ff1e6de18448b5

> A new function like `std::vectorAE::AESinkInfo CActiveAESink::GetDriverSinks(std::string_view driver) would help remove many copies (new and existing) of code similar to

Maybe but is not really related to this PR

> A proper split function in CAESinkFactory::ParseDevice(), like in commit https://github.com/lrusak/xbmc/commit/040262f0367127a6634b0ab821ff1e6de18448b5

Note that `CAESinkFactory::ParseDevice` is not a regular string split only: driver and friendlyName are optional and also is check that driver is valid string:  i.e: if you change/hack WASAPI or DIRECTSOUND name stored in settings then is considered no valid and driver reset to "".

> The logic to find a sink with same friendly name or first/default sink of same driver is duplicated in the sink opening and the audio setting filler. Maybe could be solved by generalizing the arguments and extracting to shared functions.

Added a fourth commit that consolidates the changes in one place and improves some things. If accepted, the third commit replaces the previous two (can be squashed). The basic functionality is the same but with improvements:

- No attempt is made to open the audio device the first time if it is already known not to exist.
- Saving settings changes is not delayed until the user enters in settings.
- The friendly name is also monitored, in case it changes keeping the same device name (this case was not contemplated in the previous commits).
- The logic is in one place so prevents future inconsistencies if it is modified/improved.

I like the last commit, is there a reason why the device is not validated in CActiveAESink::OpenSink()?
(thinking about a system update  or maybe an output plugged or unplugged while Kodi is running)
I don't have hdmi to test what happens during resolution / refresh rate change, we wouldn't want the validation to fail and find another device for a temporary and expected unavailability of an output.

> is there a reason why the device is not validated in CActiveAESink::OpenSink()?

The main purpose is to validate the settings and this only needs to be done once when the settings are loaded.

> (thinking about a system update or maybe an output plugged or unplugged while Kodi is running)
> I don't have hdmi to test what happens during resolution / refresh rate change, we wouldn't want the validation to fail and find another device for a temporary and expected unavailability of an output.

There are other different cases when device change events occur that are also taken into account. The current design already reloads the settings and re-enumerates audio devices and then `ValidateOutputDevices()` is also called again.

If devices changes occur while Kodi is running they are considered "temporary events" and the saved settings are NOT modified (but allows temporarily use another audio device). Whereas if the audio device (saved in settings) is already missing when Kodi is launched it is considered a permanent change and new "alternative" audio device is saved in settings.

All this theoretically should work fine but it is not possible to test it 100% until it is used on different HW with different settings.

If you disable the configured WASAPI passthrough audio device from Windows device manager this triggers that logic and `ValidateOutputDevices` is called and fallback to another audio device but not saved in settings. If you enable again is configured again, etc.. without altering saved settings.

**EDIT:** 
Runtime tested with latest updates in Intel NUC8i3BEK using passthrough in combination with display refresh rate change and Windows HDR on/off events and all seems working as planned, no issues found due AE changes. No unexpected device changes (even temporary) are shown in the logs.

After testing and thinking about it some more, I think there are a couple problems with the last commit's approach:

- it's not a good idea to change the setting automatically because it will cause problems when Kodi is started before a TV or receiver is considered active by Windows. The settings device won't be found and changed to the default device of the same driver, when the device is turned back on, the setting won't change back.

- Some calls to LoadSettings() are followed by ValidateOutputDevices() and others are not. The reason why not is not clear to me, and unless that reason is written down somewhere, it will be easy to make a mistake in future extensions. Could the validation be integrated inside LoadSettings() so it is always done?

- If the settings device fails to open with CAESinkFactory::Create(), the previous version tried to Create() with the alternative devices. Seemed like a good idea but I don't know if it would help in real situations. This last version doesn't allow it but it could be re-added: ValidateOutputDevice() could return a list of devices instead of a single name. ValidateOutputDevices would use the first one, and CAESinkFactory::Create() could loop over all the names until one works or the list is exhausted.

> it's not a good idea to change the setting automatically because it will cause problems when Kodi is started before a TV or receiver is considered active by Windows. The settings device won't be found and changed to the default device of the same driver, when the device is turned back on, the setting won't change back.

Steps to reproduce this? in my system audio devices still enumerated when TV and AVR are turned off. Maybe you confused with "open device" but now (with latest commit) only validates that setting device stills enumerated.

However, this PR is not intended to fix problems when the TV or AVR turned off. Only fixes issues when device names change (permanently) due to driver updates.

> Some calls to LoadSettings() are followed by ValidateOutputDevices() and others are not. The reason why not is not clear to me, and unless that reason is written down somewhere, it will be easy to make a mistake in future extensions. Could the validation be integrated inside LoadSettings() so it is always done?

The reason is: only validates settings when is called `LoadSettings()` AND devices are enumerated i.e is a call to
`m_sink.EnumerateSinkList(false, "");` as if sink List are empty is useless compare settings names with nothing :)

> If the settings device fails to open with CAESinkFactory::Create(), the previous version tried to Create() with the alternative devices. Seemed like a good idea but I don't know if it would help in real situations. This last version doesn't allow it but it could be re-added: ValidateOutputDevice() could return a list of devices instead of a single name. ValidateOutputDevices would use the first one, and CAESinkFactory::Create() could loop over all the names until one works or the list is exhausted.

Maybe in a follow-up PR, I don't have more time right now....

> However, this PR is not intended to fix problems when the TV or AVR turned off. Only fixes issues when device names change (permanently) due to driver updates.

Not always easy to distinguish permanent and temporary.
1/ Device available with same driver / friendly name: OK to save, we are reasonably sure it's the same device. That's the main case of the PR.
2/ Device available with same driver / device GUID / different friendly name: maybe OK, at least the GUID is common. Is that what happens when plugging a different device in the same hdmi port? I don't have hardware to test. If yes then would be OK to save.

3/ Rules that look for default or first device of same driver, or any driver: dangerous and outside of the PR scope. The new device has nothing in common with original, the situation doesn't happen as consequence of a driver update, it will change the selected device without the user consent. We could end up there because something is turned off / unplugged. I don't think it's ok to save the updated setting.

Agreed that fixing the device off case is not in the scope of the PR but it shouldn't be made possibly worse. I'm not affected by that problem but can only imagine Kodi has a problem because the expected device cannot be enumerated on start. If the setting is not saved for 3/ maybe the PR helps a little with more relaxed rules to match the setting to an enumerated device.

> > Some calls to LoadSettings() are followed by ValidateOutputDevices() and others are not. The reason why not is not clear to me, and unless that reason is written down somewhere, it will be easy to make a mistake in future extensions. Could the validation be integrated inside LoadSettings() so it is always done?
> 
> The reason is: only validates settings when is called `LoadSettings()` AND devices are enumerated i.e is a call to `m_sink.EnumerateSinkList(false, "");` as if sink List are empty is useless compare settings names with nothing :)

ok, then should the validation be added inside the enumeration?

Even I can't reproduce the problems you mention, I modified conditions to save only in case of same device: 

Same driver and same friendly name with different GUID (main use case of PR) or same name GUID with different friendly name (same GUID is same audio device for sure because GUID are unique).

In all others cases (switch from WASAPI to DIRECTSOUND, or from WASAPI:x to WASAPI:default, etc.) is allowed use device temporally but changes are not saved.

> ok, then should the validation be added inside the enumeration?

Really not because when devices are enumerated settings are not yet loaded 

...and I don't see the need to do this either (add methods inside others).

Thanks, it's in pretty good shape and almost finished as far as I am concerned, with just the one style comment left.
Functionality seems OK and safe. You could squash the last commits / rewrite the commit messages for a last look.
A non-Windows review would be good but there is plenty of time to backtrack before v21 release if necessary.

@fritsch 
If you have something important to say, now is probably the time. If no one says anything against it, I will merge it on Sunday since it solves an important issue on Windows and it would be nice if it could be tested in Alpha 3. Although I think that the risk of break something on other platforms is minimal.
This should probably be tested on a few other platforms before merging.

> This should probably be tested on a few other platforms before merging.

Just knowing the format of the audio device string stored in `guisettings.xml` on the other platforms would help to guess if it might cause problems.

Android already tested.
I followed the discussion. All fine with me, sane argumentation. Therefore I did not jump in. Regressions we will determine ;-)
I agree with fritsch and CrystalP: refactors and code improvements better separated to easy track regressions. Then lets merge as is without changing unnecessary things for now.

only `ALSA:@` and i couldn't reactivate the correct device by selecting it in the gui. so i bisected to this commit.
now after i edit guisettings.xml manually to `ALSA:@:CARD=PCH,DEV=0` (taken from the nexus version) it's working again and i can also switch between devices.....

This PR do also remove passthrough on CoreELEC devices. So I guess also on LibreELEC.
With the fix `find_last_of` above the passthrough options looks like back again.
But on Kodi start it switch back to default audio device.
So after Kodi update with this PR included the audio device must be changed one time to work again.

Also before: `CAESinkALSA::Initialize - Opened device "surround71:CARD=AMLAUGESOUND,DEV=0"`
With this PR: `CAESinkALSA::Initialize - Opened device "surround71"`

Functions like `GetParamFromName` are broken now as no `CARD` or `DEV` is anymore included in `device`.

issue_context.title: Passthrough output device randomly reverts from WASAPI to DIRECTSOUND, killing bitstream
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

I use Kodi on Windows in combination with a Denon AV receiver that is capable of playing all manner of bitstreamed audio formats up to and including Dolby Atmos.  In order for formats like Dolby Atmos to work, you must select "WASAPI: HDMI - DENON-AVRHD" in Settings -> System -> Audio -> Passthrough output device, and then tick the checkboxes for the formats your receiver supports.  In my case, all of them.

I leave "Audio output device" in the same area (System -> Settings -> Audio) set to "DIRECTSOUND: HDMI - DENON-AVRHD" as this provides the best compatibility for Kodi interface sounds.  However, this is a separate setting from "Passthrough output device"

## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

The passthrough output device in Settings -> System -> Audio should keep its setting.

Root cause of this is that audio device name configured in Kodi is not available during some instants due power on/off devices sequence or due HDMI handshake issues.

If audio device configured is not available then "by design" Kodi fallbacks to another available audio device.

Some workarounds are possible:

Always power on TV and AVR first Kodi last.
Always power off Kodi first, TV and AVR last.

> you must select "WASAPI: HDMI - DENON-AVRHD" in Settings -> System -> Audio -> Passthrough output device

Not necessarily. You can select `WASAPI: default`  as long one default audio device always exists (name not changes) is less probably Kodi can not access to audio device because "this name not exist". Then in Windows Control Panel settings configure the default audio device to one you want use. 

Kodi always points to "default" and Windows assigns "default" to a physical device.

> I leave "Audio output device" in the same area (System -> Settings -> Audio) set to "DIRECTSOUND: HDMI - DENON-AVRHD" as this provides the best compatibility for Kodi interface sounds.

This is not necessary. You can/should use the same `WASAPI: default` here. As long Kodi sounds are PCM they will be sent as is using the same WASAPI device (WASAPI can be used for everything passthrough / no passthrough).

If all of the above is not enough, you can disable all audio devices from Windows > Device Manager except the one you want to use. Kodi cannot switch to another audio device if there is only one.

It actually is necessary as I mentioned for the "best compatibility".  While WASAPI can work, DIRECTSOUND works better.  Why? Because of the HDMI silent stream bug.  I use a program called Sound Keeper to keep the HDMI audio stream from going into a sleep state.  If you don't do something like this, the first X seconds of any interface sound or video is cut off while the AVR figures out what audio format is being played.

And yes, I'm aware that the exact functionality Sound Keeper provides is built into Kodi.  But that doesn't fix the same problem happening on the computer when Kodi isn't being used, for example playing YouTube video through FIrefox.

So again, the best compatibility - the most seamless experience - is using a combination of Sound Keeper and Kodi's interface sounds in "DIRECTSOUND" mode.  You get no missing audio or pops from the sound system when using an AVR.
